dedupe_keys.name: fiji bureau of statistics 2017 population and housing census household characteristics by tikina an arcgis feature service with dwelling type tenure land tenure roof wall and floor materials wall condition and rooms

description: The Fiji Bureau of Statistics publishes 2017 census dashboards built on ArcGIS Online, linked from its census dashboard page. The Household Characteristics dashboard draws on a public feature service of 86 tikina (district) polygons with ADM codes. For every tikina it counts households by type of living quarters, tenure of quarters and land tenure, by floor, roof and wall material, by wall condition and by number of rooms, each split into urban and rural. In Namosi tikina, for example, all 209 households live in detached one-family houses. A separate two-row table gives national shares of drinking water source, toilet facility, cooking fuel and waste disposal by sex of household head, with 61.7 percent of male-headed households on metered water piped into the dwelling. Coverage is national. Format and access: open ArcGIS REST queries returning JSON or GeoJSON, plus PDF census releases, no registration. Licence: not stated on the pages read. Caveats: water, toilet and fuel data were not found at tikina level; some field aliases are duplicated in the urban wall columns. Simulation uses: cyclone and flood damage models needing roof and wall materials and wall condition by district. Related records: a Fiji building wind damage record for cyclone Winston.

name: Fiji Bureau of Statistics 2017 Population and Housing Census household characteristics by tikina, an ArcGIS feature service with dwelling type, tenure, land tenure, roof, wall and floor materials, wall condition and rooms
schema_summary: Per tikina (ADM1 to ADM3 names and P-codes), total, urban and rural counts of households by living quarters type (detached one-family house, house of multiple small structures, apartment building, dwelling attached to shop, lodging, hotel, other), tenure of quarters, land tenure (freehold, state lease, iTLTB lease, village tenure, squatting and others), floor, roof and wall material (wood, masonite, metal, concrete, traditional, tent), wall condition (good, average, poor) and number of rooms. The CH_6 table gives national percentages of drinking water source, toilet facility, cooking fuel and waste disposal by sex of household head.
